verdict: AST SpaceMobile's revenue nearly tripled to $42.3M as gateway deliveries and U.S. government milestones ramped up — but it still lost $132M for shareholders, spending about $5 to run the business for every $1 of revenue while it builds its satellite constellation.

kpis.label: 2026 revenue guidance
kpis.note: reaffirmed, with upside from recent contracts

segments.name: Products
segments.note: Gateway equipment delivered to commercial and government customers, including $1.4M from a related party.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Services revenue, mostly U.S. government milestones met during the quarter.

flow.costPlain: What it costs to deliver the gateways and services sold this quarter — $22.5M for products and $2.9M for services.

opex.name: Engineering services costs
opex.note: Engineers designing and building the satellite network — the biggest running cost, more than twice revenue.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Running the company — legal, finance and admin.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Research into the next generation of satellites and technology.

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of satellites, factories and equipment over their useful lives.

opex.name: Loss on involuntary conversion
opex.note: A small loss from an asset damaged or destroyed and replaced through insurance.

follow100Note: For every $100 of revenue, AST spent about $499 running the business. The $406 shortfall is covered by cash on hand. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Revenue is ramping, from a tiny base
takeaways.text: Revenue hit $42.3M, up from $14.7M a year ago, driven by gateway deliveries and U.S. government milestones. The company stayed on track for $150–200M of revenue for the full year, with upside from contracts signed recently.

takeaways.title: A fortress balance sheet buys time
takeaways.text: Cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash totalled about $3.2B at quarter-end. On top of that, Japan's Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications is providing about $1.0B of non-dilutive funding for midband satellites, and a further ~$1.2B pipeline of U.S. quasi-government financing is in the works for 2027.

takeaways.title: The constellation is the whole bet
takeaways.text: Production is running through BlueBird 51, with a target of about 45 satellites in orbit by mid-2027 and launch agreements covering more than 100 BlueBirds across 2027–2028. AST also announced Blacklift, its own 20-ton reusable rocket, to launch up to five satellites at a time starting in late 2028.

oneTimers: Stock-based compensation was $52.3M in the quarter — more than revenue. Adjusted operating expenses, which exclude it, depreciation and the conversion loss, were $133.6M.
The $0.05M loss on involuntary conversion this quarter compares with a $125.9M loss in Q2 2026, which is why total operating expenses fell from $329.1M to $211.0M quarter over quarter.
otherDetail: Other expense of $6.9M, net: interest expense of $30.3M was almost entirely offset by interest income of $30.1M on the company's large cash balance, plus $6.7M of other expense, net.
footerNote: Net loss of $171.8M is before allocating $39.4M to noncontrolling interests; the loss attributable to common stockholders was $132.4M ($0.44 per Class A share). This is a loss quarter: the shortfall is covered by the company's cash on hand.
